title: Least-Favorable Mixtures and Optimal Tests for Rosenbaum Sharp-Null Sensitivity Analysis
banked_reason: Math PASS, but the finite LP diagnostic and fixed-record Q-known oracle boundary remain below the requested field novelty floor after directed revision and independent validity gating.
gap_reasons: The asserted terminal-block contribution is an LP-duality equivalence for a self-selected support family (D_B=D_V), but the positioning identifies no closest published terminal-block/least-favorable-support workflow or theorem that this certificate improves upon; as written it is a useful finite diagnostic, not a demonstrated field-opening Stat advance.

The Q-known fixed-record oracle boundary follows from an explicit separator below q(m)/q(1) and null-polytope membership above it; the node itself disclaims an estimator, selected statistic, new general design-sensitivity regime, or optimal exponent, so it does not independently clear the injected field novelty floor.

This counterexample has a concrete witness but names no specific published estimator, paper, or workflow that imposes the refuted coordinatewise-monotonicity restriction, so it cannot support the claimed negative-result positioning without a target comparison.
proof_attempt_summary: Stage 0 proved the pair all-tests NP frontier, the finite product-vertex LP and least-favorable-mixture dual, exact validity-region topology, a high-level m=3 support switch, a strict monotonicity-loss witness, and the fixed-Q replicated oracle boundary. The math panel passed, but directed D0.R positioning edits could not make the finite LP diagnostic or restricted oracle theorem clear the field novelty floor; an independent gpt-5.6-sol validity gate assessed the achieved tier as subfield. A follow-on field run should reuse these results as lemmas and add a genuinely implementable level-indexed procedure plus the exact joint two-sided improvement region rather than re-proposing the oracle package.
tldr: Conditioning on the observed records turns the Rosenbaum sharp-null problem into an exact finite all-tests linear program. The Rosenbaum-specific finite contribution is the product-vertex program, the indexed-support criterion \(D_{\mathcal B}=D_{\mathcal V}\), the exact classical-validity topology, and auditable support-switch certificates. In the three-position example, \(\mathcal A_1=(0,2/3]\); at level \(7/10\), the optimal rule is \((1/10,7/10,1)\), its power is \(197/260\), and the least-favorable weights are \(16/21\) and \(5/21\). A separate \(84\)-vertex diagnostic proves that coordinatewise monotonicity can cost exactly \(1/720\). In the fixed-record, fixed-score replicated oracle experiment, with positions \(1\) and \(m\) labeling the score minimum and maximum, the all-randomized-tests design-sensitivity boundary is \(\widetilde\Gamma_{\mathrm{all}}^\star(Q)=Q(m)/Q(1)\). Below it, the explicit endpoint score \(s_\Gamma(j)=\mathbf1\{j=m\}-\Gamma\mathbf1\{j=1\}\) yields uniform null size and alternative-error bounds \(e^{-c_0n}\), where \(c_0=\Delta^2/[2(\Gamma+1)^2]\); at and above it, the frontier equals \(\alpha\) for every \(n\). For \(m=2\), the boundary is \(Q(2)/Q(1)=q_2/(1-q_2)\), the sign/McNemar success odds.
gap: Generic finite minimax theory does not expose the Rosenbaum product vertices, decide when a prescribed indexed terminal-block support is sufficient, identify the levels where the classical tilt is minimax sharp, or provide exact support-switch certificates. Existing asymptotic sensitivity results study selected procedures or sensitivity-value estimators rather than the maximal common-\(\Gamma\) detectability boundary over every randomized test.
fill: Vertex reduction makes composite-null validity finitely auditable. Linear-program duality and complementary slackness give the least-favorable mixture, assignment-dependent likelihood-ratio ties, the support equality \(D_{\mathcal B}=D_{\mathcal V}\), the tie-block representation of \(\mathcal A_n\), and the affine support-switch envelope. In the replicated design, the explicit endpoint score \(s_\Gamma(j)=\mathbf1\{j=m\}-\Gamma\mathbf1\{j=1\}\) has null supremum zero and alternative mean \(\Delta=[Q(m)-\Gamma Q(1)]/\sum_kQ(k)\). Hoeffding's inequality then gives both errors at most \(e^{-c_0n}\), while \(q\in\mathcal P_m(\Gamma)\) at and above the boundary gives the exact all-tests converse.
